run.question: A customer reported an order failure with trace ID TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR. Can you search across all our app-190-service-* indexes to trace the request flow and find where the error originated? What error code was returned?

report.summary: The trace ID TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR appears in all four app-190-service-* indices and is fully reconstructable from logs: gateway received POST /api/orders for user_12847 (04:49:00.000Z), auth authenticated that user via JWT (04:49:00.010Z, INFO), orders started processing SKU-78234 quantity 500 (04:49:00.030Z, INFO), and then the inventory service emitted the first error, error_code INV-ERR-4082: 'Failed to reserve stock for SKU-78234: insufficient inventory. Requested: 500, Available: 23' (04:49:00.080Z). Orders then failed with ORD-ERR-1001 ('Order failed: inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082'), and the gateway returned GW-ERR-400 'Request failed with 400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled', i.e. HTTP 400, to the caller. So the error originated in the inventory service's stock reservation for SKU-78234, and the code returned to the customer at the edge was GW-ERR-400 / HTTP 400 (inventory's own code INV-ERR-4082). The failure is isolated: in the 24h authorized window the four indices hold 206 documents with only 3 ERROR documents, exactly the three error codes of this one trace, and inventory logged 50 successful stock reservations in the sampled hour including another successful reservation for TRACE-41085 in the same second. No Kubernetes objects for inventory/orders/auth exist in this cluster and Jaeger/Prometheus were unavailable, so no span graph, metric error-rate or pod-level confirmation was possible; ordering is from log timestamps, not span parent references.

claims.text: The index pattern app-190-service-* matches four indices — app-190-service-auth, app-190-service-gateway, app-190-service-inventory and app-190-service-orders — and all four map the same fields: @timestamp, duration_ms, error_code, level, message, service, span_id, trace_id.

Exactly six log records carry trace_id TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR, all on 2026-11-21 between 04:49:00.000Z and 04:49:00.140Z: gateway 'Received request POST /api/orders for user_12847' (INFO, span-gw-err); auth 'User user_12847 authenticated via JWT token' (INFO, span-auth-err); orders 'Processing order for product SKU-78234, quantity: 500' (INFO, span-orders-err); inventory ERROR INV-ERR-4082 (span-inv-err); orders ERROR ORD-ERR-1001 (span-orders-err-2); gateway ERROR GW-ERR-400 (span-gw-err-2).

The first error in the flow is from service inventory at 2026-11-21T04:49:00.080Z with error_code INV-ERR-4082 and message 'Failed to reserve stock for SKU-78234: insufficient inventory. Requested: 500, Available: 23'; this is the origin of the failure, a stock-quantity rejection, and it is the only occurrence of the phrase 'insufficient inventory' in the whole 24h authorized window.
The orders service propagated the dependency error verbatim: ORD-ERR-1001 'Order failed: inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082' at 04:49:00.130Z (span-orders-err-2).

The gateway's response for this request carries error_code GW-ERR-400 with message 'Request failed with 400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled' at 04:49:00.140Z, i.e. the customer received HTTP 400 with gateway error code GW-ERR-400.

The failure is isolated to this trace: across the full 24h authorized window the four indices hold 206 documents, of which 203 are INFO and 3 are ERROR, and in the 1h window ending 05:15:31Z the ERROR documents group to one each for services gateway, inventory and orders with error codes GW-ERR-400, INV-ERR-4082 and ORD-ERR-1001.

The inventory service was otherwise succeeding: its index returned 51 documents in the 04:25:00.080Z–05:14:00.080Z span, 50 of them INFO 'Stock reserved successfully', and a second reservation in the same second (04:49:00.080Z, trace_id TRACE-41085) succeeded, so the inventory service itself was not broadly down.

The auth service shows no failure for this trace: its only document with trace_id TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR is INFO 'User user_12847 authenticated via JWT token' with duration_ms 15 and no error_code, and no ERROR document exists for service auth in the window.

The services inventory, orders, auth and gateway named in these logs have no Kubernetes objects in this cluster: the Service list (29 services) and Deployment list (25 deployments) contain no inventory/orders/auth entries and the only app-102a workload is api-gateway-585c5579f6-cx4ch in namespace app-102a, while the rest are otel-demo workloads, so no pod status, container termination reason or container log could be read for these app-190 services.

Injected fault flags were considered as the cause and rejected for these services: the otel-demo flagd ConfigMap 'flagd-config' lists only productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, each with defaultVariant 'off' and none targeting inventory, orders, gateway or auth.

Cluster events in the window (grouped by involvedObject.kind, namespace and reason) involve only Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod objects in app-102a, kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo, plus Node and Lease objects; no event references the inventory, orders or auth services, so events provide no evidence about this failure.

The proximate cause is a stock shortfall for SKU-78234 (23 units available against a single order for 500 units), meaning the requested order quantity exceeded on-hand inventory at that moment; why the on-hand quantity was 23, and whether the 500-unit quantity is abnormal for this product, is not shown by any log or metric I could read.

gaps: No span-level trace graph: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE and traces_query_trace_by_id for 'TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR' returned INVALID_PARAMS because that value is not a hexadecimal Jaeger trace ID; therefore parent-child call edges are inferred only from the trace_id field and @timestamp ordering in the logs, not from span parent references.

No Prometheus telemetry for these services: get_label_values for service_name on traces_span_metrics_calls_total returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no own error-rate or latency reading exists for inventory, orders, gateway or auth; ERROR series for them are unknown rather than zero.

No Kubernetes objects exist for the app-190 services (inventory, orders, auth, gateway) in this cluster, so pod phase, restart counts, last termination reason, container logs and resource shortfalls could not be inspected for those services.

The stock level history for SKU-78234 and the origin of the 23-unit availability (depletion, reservation by another order, or an intentionally low stock seed) are not observable in the available sources; no metric or log documents inventory quantity over time.

Whether an order for 500 units is normal traffic or an anomalous/test order is unknown: only one 'Processing order for product' log exists in the 24h window, so other orders' quantities cannot be compared.

Kubernetes objects were read at 05:15–05:16Z after the incident and cannot prove the cluster state at 04:49:00Z; the change_history integration is not available, so no audit of configuration changes during the window could be checked.
next_steps: Check the inventory/WMS system of record for SKU-78234 around 2026-11-21T04:49:00Z to confirm the 23-unit on-hand figure and whether a replenishment or reservation race produced it.
Review whether the 500-unit order quantity was legitimate (customer/load-generator behaviour) and whether the orders service should pre-validate quantity against stock before creating an order.
Add distributed tracing and Prometheus instrumentation for the app-190 services so inventory/orders/gateway failure rates and latency can be checked directly rather than only from logs.
